note: Dated catalogue of models the router can pick from. Ids go stale: run `fo.py refresh` to see drift against what your CLIs offer today, and override entries in ~/.config/frontier-orchestration/roster.json instead of editing this file.

fable.description: Alias for the top Claude tier (Claude Fable 5.2 on 2026-11-15, 1M context). Hardest reasoning, difficult code, long-horizon agentic work. Highest Claude price and long turns: use it where a mistake is expensive.

opus.description: Alias for the current Claude Opus (Opus 5.5 on 2026-11-15, 1M context). One tier below fable at about half the price. Best default for orchestration, holding a whole codebase in view, and long prose that must stay accurate.

sonnet.description: Alias for mid-tier Claude (Sonnet 5.5 on 2026-11-15, 1M context). Fast, capable, much cheaper than frontier. Best for well-specified bulk work: repo sweeps, mechanical edits, following an exact recipe.

haiku.description: Alias for the smallest Claude (Haiku 5.5 on 2026-11-15). Cheapest and fastest. For trivial mechanical steps where an error is obvious and cheap.

gpt-6.2-sol.description: Newest Sol in the Codex catalogue (GPT-6.2 Sol, first seen 2026-11-17): the vendor's fast go-to model for coding and everyday work. A DIFFERENT vendor from Claude. NO measured review prior and no evidence here that it reviews better than gpt-6.1-sol. Use it as an extra blind lane next to a measured reviewer; verify every finding.

gpt-6.2-astra.description: Newest Astra in the Codex catalogue (GPT-6.2 Astra, first seen 2026-11-17): the vendor calls it its most capable model for complex coding and professional work. A DIFFERENT vendor from Claude. NO measured review prior and no evidence here that it reviews better than gpt-6-astra. Use it as an extra blind lane next to a measured reviewer; verify every finding.

gpt-6.1-sol.description: Codex frontier (GPT-6.1 Sol), the Sol with measured runs; gpt-6.2-sol is newer and not measured. A DIFFERENT vendor from Claude, so it fails differently. Maintainer runs: on server-side concurrency and data-safety code review every finding held, most with its own runtime probe; it found transaction-lifetime, lock-order and timeout defects. It did not catch that one of its own prescribed fixes crashed the driver: verify prescribed fixes by reproduction.

gpt-6-astra.description: Codex frontier (GPT-6 Astra), the Astra with measured runs; gpt-6.2-astra is newer and not measured. A DIFFERENT vendor from Claude. Finds CONCRETE DEFECTS: a wrong line in the code. Maintainer runs: on a raw estimate 3 of 5 specific claims held and its size asks were about 2.5x too big; on an already-verified estimate its direction held on every item and about one third of its size asks survived. Verify both the claim and the size.

gpt-6-sol.description: Previous-generation general Codex model (GPT-6 Sol). A DIFFERENT vendor from Claude. No measured review prior of its own: prefer gpt-6.1-sol or gpt-6-astra for a ship gate.

gpt-5.6-sol.description: Previous Codex frontier. Finds MISSING CATEGORIES and framing errors rather than wrong lines. Maintainer runs: on a raw estimate framing and sizes both held; on a verified estimate framing held but about one twelfth of its size asks survived. On a high-stakes review, run it beside Astra: neither finds the other's class of problem.

gpt-6.1-terra.description: Current mid-tier Codex (GPT-6.1 Terra). Bounded implementation and mechanical work at lower cost. No measured review prior.

gpt-5.6-terra.description: Older mid-tier Codex. Kept for runs that measured it; prefer gpt-6.1-terra.

gpt-6-luna.description: Fast, affordable Codex model for easier tasks (GPT-6 Luna). Cheap bounded checks. No measured review prior.

gpt-reserve.description: Fast, affordable agentic coding model from the Codex catalogue. No measured prior.

gpt-5.6-luna.description: Older fast, cheap Codex model. Prefer gpt-6-luna.

gemini-4-argon.description: Top Gemini (Google). A DIFFERENT vendor from Claude and Codex. Strong at long context and multimodal input (images, video, PDFs). Maintainer runs on content and visual work only: screenshot reading 42 of 63 claims held, visual defects 10 of 10 held, and one spec-review finding was invented (it quoted figures the artefact does not have). No measured prior for code review: verify every finding. An optional third blind review lane.

gemini-4-hydrogen.description: New Gemini (Google), effort up to xhigh. A DIFFERENT vendor from Claude and Codex. NO measured prior and no evidence that it is better than gemini-4-argon. Use it only as an extra blind lane next to a measured reviewer; verify every finding.

gemini-3.8-flash.description: Fast Gemini (Google). A DIFFERENT vendor from Claude and Codex. No measured prior. For cheap bounded checks and long-context skims.

jev.description: System One judge (TypeSafe Jev, or an OpenJev-compatible server). Typed judgments and calibrated probabilities, never text. For routing, scoring and yes/no judgments that code acts on.
